H1: Employment status may predict daily free time.

H2: Daily free time may predict collectivistic and individualistic attitudes.

## 1. Load the package and data

```{r load, message=FALSE}
#load the codebook package
library(codebook)

#load data/raw/data_doctored.csv
raw <- read.csv("Data/Raw/data_doctored.csv")

#check row and column counts, and inspect the first few rows
dim(raw)
str(raw)

#make data with ID, employment status, daily free time, collectivistic and individulistic attitudes; keep raw unchanged

Gdata <- raw[,c("ResponseId",
               "Employment", 
               "Time_free_1",
               "Individualism_col_1","Individualism_col_2","Individualism_col_3","Individualism_col_4")]

dim(Gdata)
str(Gdata)






```


## 2. Check participant IDs

```{r participant_ids}

#count na
sum(is.na(Gdata$ResponseId))
#count blank
sum(Gdata$ResponseId=="",na.rm=TRUE) #rm means remove, remove the na when do this sum because we have checked the na
#count duplicates
sum(duplicated(Gdata$ResponseId)) #to do these steps, can also run summary(data$ResponseId) in the Console
#inspect records with missing or blank IDs
missingID <- which(is.na(Gdata$ResponseId)) #and then run missingID in the Console, and can find the missingID.
print(Gdata[missingID,])
# and also, can run data[missingID,] in the Counsole, then the row of missingID will show

#remove the known empty record with no ID, then check the row count
Gdata <- Gdata[!is.na(Gdata$ResponseId),]
#! means reverse, that means if I do not have this, the code above will only leave the na data and delete all of the other data
```


## 3. Recode employment status

```{r employment status}
# codebook: 1 = Full-time, 2 = Part-time, 3 = Self-employed, 4 = Unemployed, 5 = Student, 6 = Retired
table(Gdata$Employment,useNA="ifany")
#turn Employment into a factor with labels
Gdata$Employment <- factor(Gdata$Employment,
                         levels = c(1,2,3,4,5,6),
                         labels = c("Full-time","Part-time","Self-employed","Unemployed","Student","Retired"))

# Here I decided do not use the data of the participant who chose multiple Employment status, as multiple Employment can be a confusion of the impact of Employment on the daily free time. Meanwhile, some of the combinations looks "unreasonable", for example, some participants chose "student" and "full-time" at the same time, we cannot know the true situation of them (if they are a person with full-time job but still studying something in school? Or they are srudents mainly but are near to their graduation thus they have a full-time job? -- there are so many possibilities of these situations.)

table(Gdata$Employment,useNA="ifany")
# rerun this and to see the numbers of the participants in each employment status
```

## 4. Validate daily free time

```{r daily free time}



#see summary of variables
summary(Gdata$Time_free_1)

#count NAs
sum(is.na(Gdata[,"Time_free_1"]))

#leave the total NA if any item is missing
str(Gdata[, "Time_free_1"])




#make Gh1Data with ID, Employment, and daily free time
Gh1Data <- Gdata[!is.na(Gdata$Time_free_1) & !is.na(Gdata$Employment),
               c("ResponseId","Employment","Time_free_1")]


```


## 5. Validate Collectiveistic and individualistic attitudes

```{r collectivism_vars}
#group all four Individualism_col_ variables

# Here's a little bit weird -- if the values of this variable is higher, it means that the participant has a greater collectivism, but in the database, this variable was measured by items called "Indicidualism". Thus there's maybe a little bit confict, but the two things are the same.

collect_vars <- c("Individualism_col_1","Individualism_col_2","Individualism_col_3","Individualism_col_4")


#see summary of variables
summary(Gdata[,collect_vars])


#count NAs
colSums(is.na(Gdata[,collect_vars]))

#calculate total score; leave the total NA if any item is missing
str(Gdata[, collect_vars])

Gdata[, collect_vars] <- lapply(Gdata[, collect_vars], function(x) {
  x[x == "-99" | x == -99] <- NA
  x
})

Gdata[, collect_vars] <- lapply(Gdata[, collect_vars], function(x) as.numeric(as.character(x)))

Gdata$collectTotal <- rowSums(Gdata[,collect_vars],na.rm=FALSE) #na.ra=FALSE is to remove the na, this is vital
summary(Gdata$collectTotal)


#make Gh2Data with ID, daily free time, and collect
Gh2Data <- Gdata[!is.na(Gdata$Time_free_1) & !is.na(Gdata$collectTotal),
               c("ResponseId","Time_free_1","collectTotal")]
  
summary(Gh2Data$Time_free_1)
summary(Gh2Data$collectTotal)
######## do not have results, check ##########


```


## 6. Check the final tables

```{r final_tables}
#check rows, columns, types, and missing values in Gh1Data
#one row per participant, one column per variable
dim(Gh1Data)
str(Gh1Data)
head(Gh1Data)
colSums(is.na(Gh1Data))
table(Gh1Data$Employment,useNA="ifany")
range(Gh1Data$Time_free_1)
sum(duplicated(Gh1Data$ResponseId))

#repeat the checks for Gh2Data
dim(Gh2Data)
str(Gh2Data)
head(Gh2Data)
colSums(is.na(Gh2Data))
range(Gh2Data$Time_free_1)
range(Gh2Data$collectTotal)
sum(duplicated(Gh2Data$ResponseId))
```

## 7. Add labels and generate codebooks

The descriptions come from the original codebook and our scoring decisions.
`compact_codebook()` adds summaries from the actual data. Knit the Rmd to
display the formatted codebooks.

```{r variable_labels}
#add a description to each Gh1Data column, in column order
#include the source codes, meaning, and units
var_label(Gh1Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "Employment: original codes 1=Full-time, 2=Part-time, 3=Self-employed, 4= Unemployed, 5=Student, 6=Retired; now stored as a factor",
  "daily free time; 0-360 hours; zero is valid"
)

#add a description to each Gh2Data column, in column order
#include response anchors and the commitment scoring rule
var_label(Gh2Data) <- c(
  "Unique participant ID (ResponseId)",
  "daily free time; 0-360 hours; zero is valid",
  "collectivism: mean of Individualism_col_1-4 responses, each 1=Definitrly disagree to 7=Definitely agree; no reverse coding"
)

```



```{r h1_codebook}
#generate the h1Data codebook
compact_codebook(Gh1Data)

```


```{r h2_codebook}
#generate the h2Data codebook
compact_codebook(Gh2Data)

```

## 9. Save the final tables

```{r save}
#create data/processed_data if needed
dir.create("data/processed_data",recursive=T,showWarnings=F)

#save Gh1Data and Gh2Data without an extra row-number column
write.csv(Gh1Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv",row.names=F)
write.csv(Gh2Data,"data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv",row.names=F)

#read the files back and confirm their dimensions
h1Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h1.csv")
h2Saved <- read.csv("data/processed_data/practice_h2.csv")
dim(h1Saved)
dim(h2Saved)

```
